title: Overnight oats that actually hold you
summary: Assembled in three minutes the night before. The Greek yogurt is doing the work - this lands around 30 g of protein instead of the 8 g a plain oats jar gives you.

ingredients.note: Or whatever sweetener you keep - this is purely for taste.

steps: Put the oats, chia, cinnamon and salt in a jar or bowl and stir them together dry.
Add the yogurt, milk, sweetener and vanilla. Mix properly - go right to the bottom, the chia clumps if you do not.
Cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours, ideally overnight.
In the morning it will be thick. Loosen with a splash of milk, then top with berries and a spoon of nut butter.
tips: The ratio that matters is 1 part oats to 2 parts total liquid-plus-yogurt. Everything else is negotiable.
Make three jars on Sunday - they keep 4 days and get better on day two.
Frozen berries work fine and thaw overnight in the jar. Stir them in rather than putting them on top and they turn the whole thing purple, which is either good or bad depending on your mood.
Steel-cut oats do not work here. They stay gritty. Rolled oats only.
health_notes: Swap the honey for stevia or monk fruit drops and this drops to roughly 350 calories with zero added sugar. The chia adds about 5 g of fibre and thickens the jar without any flour.

source.adapted: Standard overnight oats, rebalanced towards protein by using Greek yogurt as the base rather than milk alone.
